introduction_markdown:
Answer both questions beginning each answer on a new page in the answer booklet. Both answers carry equal marks.

Credit will be given for accuracy, correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.

Use blue ink only.

You are reminded of the necessity for orderly presentation of your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
*Using a tense suitable to your chosen topic, write an essay in French, of at least 140 and not more than 150 words, (not counting figures, words in brackets, abbreviations and names of people or places) on ONE of the following topics.*

*Credit will be given for the correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.*

*If you choose topic (b), your name must be Tume and your address GHS Nyakom.* ***The usual introduction to the letter must not be more than 20 words.***

*Use of a different name and /or address will be seriously penalised. This holds true for details that can help reveal your true identity, school and/or family.*

*If you choose topic (c), your essay must be based on the picture.*

*Off-topic material will earn no marks.*

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Un voleur qui troublait tout votre quartier venait d'être arrêté par la police.

- Décrivez les circonstances de son arrestation.
- Dites quelles ont été les réactions des uns et des autres.
- Comment s'est terminée la scène ?
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Tense chosen:** the passé composé for the events, with the imparfait for the reactions and the plus-que-parfait for what happened before the arrest. A past tense is needed because the arrest has already happened when the narrator speaks.

**Model essay** (144, or 146 if elisions are counted as two words words)

Hier matin, tout le quartier a appris que le voleur qui nous terrorisait depuis des mois avait enfin été arrêté. Il avait tenté de cambrioler une boutique à la tombée de la nuit, mais le commerçant, alerté par un bruit, avait crié au voleur. Les voisins sont sortis en courant et ont encerclé le malfaiteur. Quelques minutes plus tard, les policiers sont arrivés et lui ont passé les menottes.

Les réactions ont été très différentes. Certains habitants applaudissaient et criaient de joie, car ils pouvaient désormais dormir tranquilles. D'autres, plus prudents, estimaient qu'il fallait le laisser se défendre devant la justice. Sa mère pleurait de honte au milieu de la foule.

Le voleur a été emmené au commissariat, la tête baissée. Le tribunal le jugera bientôt. Depuis ce jour, le calme est revenu dans notre quartier et chacun remercie la police de son courage.

**Notes**

The essay covers the three bullet points: the circumstances of the arrest (an attempted burglary at dusk, neighbours and police, first paragraph), the reactions of the different people (joy, caution, the mother's shame, second paragraph) and how the scene ended (taken to the police station, calm restored, third paragraph).

**Marking criteria**

| Criterion | What earns the marks |
|---|---|
| Accuracy | Correct verb forms, agreements, spelling and accents; correct use of the tense chosen |
| Variety of expressions | Linking words (*d'abord*, *puis*, *finalement*, *heureusement*) and set phrases |
| Variety of verbs | Several different verbs instead of *être*, *avoir* and *faire* only |
| Vocabulary and idioms | Words and expressions suited to the topic; idioms used correctly |
| Relevance and length | All bullet points covered; between 140 and 150 words |

**Common mistakes**

1. Describing a different event (for example a robbery still in progress) instead of the arrest that has just taken place.
2. Forgetting one of the three bullet points, usually the last question about how the scene ended.
